questions.subtopic: 1A8 Internal audit and the Three Lines Model. What an ongoing role adds
questions.question: A Senegalese telecom's board, after the required discussion of safeguards, makes its chief audit executive permanently responsible for the data privacy office. Which step do the Standards require MOST specifically because the role is ongoing?

options.A: Set a plan to hand the role back to management
options.B: Keep third-party assurance until 12 months after the role ends
options.C: Record the duties, nature of work and safeguards in the charter
options.D: Advise the board and senior management on suitable safeguards

questions.key_concept: An ongoing role beyond internal auditing must be written into the charter: its responsibilities, the nature of the work and the safeguards.
questions.pre_read: Sort the four steps into three piles: any such role, a temporary role, an ongoing role.
questions.correct_explanation: Standard 7.1 separates two cases. For a role beyond internal auditing that continues, the chief audit executive must write the responsibilities, the nature of the work and the safeguards into the internal audit charter, which the board approves. Assurance until 12 months after the role ends, the closest choice, and a hand-back plan are the rules for a temporary role; this one has no end date. Advice on safeguards is required in both cases.

wrong_explanations.A: A plan to return the duties to management is required when the role is temporary. This role is permanent, so there is nothing to hand back.
wrong_explanations.B: Closest choice: another route to assurance is needed here too, but the 12 months after the role ends is the temporary-role rule. An ongoing role has no end date.
wrong_explanations.D: Advising the board and senior management on safeguards is required for any role that could impair independence, temporary or ongoing, and has already happened here.

tips: Eliminate: A, because a hand-back plan belongs to a temporary role, and D, because advice on safeguards is required for every such role and is already done.
Final two: C beats B because the 12 months after the role ends applies to a temporary role; the step tied to an ongoing role is documenting it in the charter.
Exam cue: for a role beyond internal auditing, read the duration first. Ongoing: charter and another route to assurance. Temporary: third-party assurance, 12 months after, and a hand-back plan.

questions.subtopic: 1A8 Internal audit and the Three Lines Model. Declining to rely on second-line work
questions.question: The finance director of a Kenyan mobile-money firm wants internal audit to rely on compliance's agent-monitoring tests, which the chief audit executive has judged too thin to support conclusions. What is the BEST course?

options.A: Decline to rely on the tests and have internal auditors retest
options.B: Rely on the tests and document the basis for doing so
options.C: Rely on the tests and leave their conclusions with compliance
options.D: Raise the lack of coordination with senior management, then the board

questions.key_concept: Reliance is the chief audit executive's choice, made after evaluating the other provider's work. Work too weak to support conclusions is retested or redone.
questions.pre_read: A basis for reliance has to exist before it can be documented. What did the evaluation of compliance's tests find?
questions.correct_explanation: Standard 9.5 asks the chief audit executive to consider relying on other providers, not to rely on them, and leaves that executive responsible for internal audit's conclusions. Its considerations add that, after evaluating the work, the chief audit executive may decide it cannot be relied on; internal auditors then retest or do the work themselves. Documenting a basis, the closest choice, is the rule when reliance is justified. Here the evaluation found none.

wrong_explanations.B: Closest choice: a documented basis is required when internal audit relies on another provider. The evaluation found the tests too thin, so there is no sound basis to record.
wrong_explanations.C: Responsibility for internal audit's conclusions stays with the chief audit executive, whoever's work they rest on. It cannot be passed to compliance.
wrong_explanations.D: A coordination concern is raised with senior management first, then the board if needed, once coordination proves out of reach. The issue here is the quality of the work.

tips: Eliminate: C, because the chief audit executive stays responsible for internal audit's conclusions, and D, because the problem is weak testing, not a failure to coordinate.
Final two: A beats B because a basis must exist before it is documented; work judged too thin to support conclusions is retested, not relied on.
Exam cue: coordinate with every assurance provider, but rely only after evaluating the work. Cost or a senior manager's wish is never the basis for reliance.

questions.subtopic: 1A8 Internal audit and the Three Lines Model. Whose follow-up is it
questions.question: The three-person internal audit function of a Norwegian fish farm is offered four standing tasks. Which task would MOST clearly be a second-line duty that could impair its independence?

options.A: Maintaining the audit universe used to plan its engagements
options.B: Running the follow-up of actions from management's risk reviews
options.C: Consolidating the assurance providers' results into one report for the board
options.D: Running the follow-up of actions from its own engagements

questions.key_concept: Internal audit follows up the actions from its own engagements. Following up actions from management's risk reviews is management's work, which it must not own.
questions.pre_read: Two options look alike. For each task, ask whose actions are being chased and who would answer if they slipped.
questions.correct_explanation: The IIA's 2026 statement on enterprise risk management draws the line by ownership. Internal audit monitors whether actions agreed in its own engagements are carried out, keeps its audit universe and brings assurance results together; all three serve its own planning and reporting. Chasing the actions from management's risk reviews is management's follow-up, which the statement says internal audit must not own. Following up its own engagements, the closest choice, is what Standard 15.2 requires.

wrong_explanations.A: The audit universe is internal audit's own planning tool: its list of what could be audited. Keeping it is part of preparing the internal audit plan.
wrong_explanations.C: The statement lists coordinating and consolidating assurance results among internal audit's own activities. It gives the board one picture without owning anyone's controls.
wrong_explanations.D: Closest choice: it looks the same, but these actions come from internal audit's own engagements. Confirming they were implemented is required by Standard 15.2.

tips: Eliminate: A, because the audit universe is internal audit's own planning tool, and C, because consolidating assurance results for the board is listed among internal audit's own activities.
Final two: B beats D because internal audit confirms actions from its own engagements, while actions from management's risk reviews are management's to follow up.
Exam cue: when two tasks look alike, ask who owns the process. Internal audit may track its own results; running management's tracking makes it part of what it audits.
